hints.title: Single Peak Verification
hints.text: A valid mountain array must have length at least 3, climb strictly to a single peak, and descend strictly from that peak.

hints.title: Two-Pointer Inward Climbing
hints.text: Start two climbers: one from the left walking uphill, and one from the right walking uphill. If the mountain is valid, they must meet at the exact same peak.

hints.title: Convergence and Boundary Check
hints.text: Increment left index while arr[left] < arr[left + 1]. Decrement right index while arr[right] < arr[right - 1]. Check that left == right and 0 < left < n - 1.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Multiple peaks or valleys violate mountain structure; single pass validation avoids complex state machine edge cases.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Two-pointer inward climb checks the entire array in a single traversal using O(1) space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should carefully check boundary conditions: peak cannot be at index 0 or index n-1, and strict inequality must hold.
complexity.notes: Flat plateaus (adjacent equal elements) correctly stop both climbers early.
